breaking_changes: Version format changed from X.Y.Z (e.g. 11.9.0) to YYYY.WW.N (e.g. 2026.39.0); pin the new format if you parse version strings from --version output, build logs, or installer metadata.
CMake configure time now requires Python 3 (find_package(Python3)); the build will fail on systems without a Python 3 interpreter available at CMake configure time.
Windows installer product version (Product.wxs.in) now derives from the date-part of the version rather than PROJECT_VERSION; installer version numbering will differ from the prior release format.

evidence.blockers: Three release-infrastructure to-dos are P0: confirming the new version format renders correctly on the server binary (c47aa2a-1), verifying the candidate prerelease publishing path works end-to-end (658d565-1), and validating the automated release branch creation workflow (bfb9dd5-1). These are foundational to the new release pipeline — if any fails, the candidate cannot ship.
evidence.breaking_changes: Three breaking changes: version string format changed (users parsing version output must adapt), Python 3 is now a hard build dependency (systems without it will fail to build), and Windows installer version numbering changed. All three were flagged by the commit review on #3539 and were coordinated with other PRs in the release pipeline. No migration is needed for end users running pre-built artifacts — only for people building from source or parsing version strings.
evidence.coverage: All 41 commits reviewed; 21 to-dos across 15 PRs rated. The release infrastructure PRs (#3539, #3579, #3580, #3581, #3588) form a cohesive set covering the new versioning scheme, weekly release branch automation, candidate artifact publishing, and website behavior. CI evidence was assessed for all entries.
evidence.manual_testing: 18 to-dos require a human with the release candidate installed. Key categories: (1) new version format display, (2) three new API surfaces — /v1/docs endpoints and lemonade_docs MCP tool (#3347), /images/edit endpoint (#3494), and wildcard origins (#3470), (3) behavioral changes on existing surfaces — /pull/variants filtering (#3198), FLM ModelScope download path (#2841), session header relay (#3510), and gpt-oss model loading (#3496), (4) website and GitHub Releases page behavior for the new prerelease channel (#3588), (5) documentation security fix for examples (#3547).
evidence.security: Wildcard origin matching (#3470) introduces new configuration syntax that should be verified against the release candidate — wildcard_port and subdomain matching are security-sensitive features. The FLM ModelScope source resolution (#2841) changes how registry_source is serialized in API responses, which could affect clients assuming a non-empty source field. The examples/ README security gap (#3547) — missing --bind 127.0.0.1 — would expose local file trees on all interfaces if followed.
